Distance Test Wrapper Function

Source: R/stat_tests.r
dist_test.Rd

Runs any of ecodive's statistical tests of a distance matrix by name, as dist_ord() does for ordination methods: does one variable, such as treatment groups, explain the differences between samples?

Usage

dist_test(dm, test, groups, data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

dm

The distances to test: a dist object such as from beta_div(), or a symmetric matrix of distances.

test

The name of a test: "anosim", "mantel", "mantel_partial", "mrpp", "permanova", or "permdisp". Flexible matching is supported (see below). Programmatic access via list_dist_tests().

groups

The variable to test: a vector with one value per sample, matched to the samples in dm by name when both are named, else in the same order as dm. Or, when data is given, the name of one of its columns (or a vector with one value per row of data). Each method takes categorical groups, numeric values, or both: see list_dist_tests().

data

Optional sample metadata: a data frame with one row per sample, holding groups (and strata) as columns. Rows are matched to the samples in dm by row name. Default: NULL.

...

Further arguments for the method's function, such as permutations, strata, seed, or cpus, which every method takes, or a method's own, such as weights for mrpp() or method (the correlation) for mantel(), or given for mantel_partial(). Each method keeps its own defaults. For mantel and mantel_partial, groups is passed as the function's y.

Value

The method's result: a list of class "ecodive_test" whose first fields are statistic, p_value, z, and n_perm. as.data.frame() turns it into one row with the same columns for every method, so results can be rbind()-ed. dist_test(dm, 'mrpp', groups, data, ...) is the same as mrpp(dm, groups, data, ...).

Details

List of Tests

Option / Function NameTest NameGroups
anosimAnalysis of Similarities (ANOSIM)categorical
mantelMantel Testnumeric
mantel_partialPartial Mantel Testnumeric
mrppMulti-Response Permutation Procedure (MRPP)categorical
permanovaPermutational Multivariate Analysis of Variancecategorical or numeric
permdispHomogeneity of Multivariate Dispersions (PERMDISP)categorical

Categorical groups are factors, character, or logical vectors; a method that takes only categorical groups gives an error for numbers, and the reverse. mantel correlates dm with the differences between samples' values, and mantel_partial does so after removing the effect of given (such as geographic distances); to compare two distance matrices, call mantel() or mantel_partial() directly. To test several variables at once, call permanova() with a formula, either directly or as dist_test(dm, 'permanova', data = meta, formula = ~ a + b).

Flexible name matching

Case insensitive and partial matching, ignoring anything but letters. E.g. test = 'PERMANOVA' or 'perma' selects permanova. Common other names also work: 'adonis' or 'adonis2' for permanova; 'betadisper' or 'PERMDISP2' for permdisp; 'Analysis of Similarities' for anosim; and 'mantel.partial' or 'partial Mantel' for mantel_partial.

Finished code should always use the full primary option name to avoid ambiguity with future additions to the list of methods.

Same names in other packages

vegan::anosim(), vegan::mantel(), and vegan::mrpp() share names with ecodive's functions, and whichever package was attached last masks the other's. Write ecodive::anosim() and so on, or use dist_test(), which always runs ecodive's, to be sure.

See also

anosim(), mantel(), mantel_partial(), mrpp(), permanova(), permdisp(), list_dist_tests()

Examples

    # 30 samples in three treatment groups. The 'high' group has more
    # of the first five genera.
    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * 20, 5), 30, 20)
    rownames(counts) <- paste0('S', 1:30)
    meta <- data.frame(
      row.names = rownames(counts),
      treatment = rep(c('ctrl', 'low', 'high'), each = 10),
      ph        = round(rnorm(30, 7, 0.3), 1) )
    high <- meta$treatment == 'high'
    counts[high, 1:5] <- counts[high, 1:5] + 5

    dm <- bray(counts)

    dist_test(dm, 'permanova', 'treatment', meta)
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 3.442, p = 0.001, z = 8.275
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.2032. Model tested as a whole:
#> 
#>          Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)    
#> Model     2   0.1813 0.2032 3.442  0.001 ***
#> Residual 27   0.7111 0.7968                 
#> Total    29   0.8924 1.0000                 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

    # Every test of treatment, as one table.
    tests <- list_dist_tests(val = 'id', groups = 'categorical')
    do.call(rbind, lapply(tests, function (m)
      as.data.frame(dist_test(dm, m, 'treatment', meta, cpus = 1)) ))
#>        test stat_name  statistic p_value         z n_perm
#> 1    anosim         R  0.3216543   0.001  6.741598    999
#> 2      mrpp     delta  0.2243903   0.001 -7.321666    999
#> 3 permanova         F  3.4422193   0.001  8.274905    999
#> 4  permdisp         F 15.6818804   0.001 13.423920    999

    # A numeric variable.
    dist_test(dm, 'adonis2', 'ph', meta)
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA)
#> 
#> F = 0.3849, p = 0.972, z = -1.488
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.01356. Model tested as a whole:
#> 
#>          Df SumOfSqs     R2     F Pr(>F)
#> Model     1   0.0121 0.0136 0.385  0.972
#> Residual 28   0.8803 0.9864             
#> Total    29   0.8924 1.0000             
    dist_test(dm, 'mantel', 'ph', meta, method = 'spearman')
#> Mantel test (Spearman)
#> 
#> r = -0.0818, p = 0.863, z = -1.089
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Correlation: Spearman's rank correlation rho
#> Alternative: greater (r is more positive than by chance)
#> Samples: 30
